title: The fruit of the Spirit (Galatians 5:22–23)
hookLine: love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control

lines: A GARDENER CAN'T MAKE AN APPLE.
FROM A TOOLBOX TO AN ORCHARD.
cards: Nobody has ever heard an apple tree grunt. It doesn't clench its branches in spring and force the apples out. It stands in the sun, drinks the rain, stays rooted, and one day the fruit is just there.
A gardener can water, prune and wait. A gardener can't make an apple. Yesterday Paul listed gifts: to one person this, to another that.
Now he writes to different churches, the churches of Galatia, and the picture changes from a toolbox to an orchard.

teach.h: THE FRUIT IS, NOT THE FRUITS ARE.
teach.b: Here's the verse in the King James: "But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, Meekness, temperance: against such there is no law." Look at the first words.

teach.h: GIFTS DIFFER; THE FRUIT IS FOR ALL.
teach.b: The fruit is. Not the fruits are. One fruit, many flavors.
Some readers hear one life growing all of these together, not a menu where you pick a favorite. Set that beside yesterday. Gifts are handed out differently: one person heals, another teaches.
Some readers add that the fruit is meant for everyone: nobody is let off love because their gift is administration. Just before, Paul lists what he calls "the works of the flesh."
Works on one side, fruit on the other. Works are made. Fruit grows.
Then the old words. Longsuffering is patience that holds out a long time. Faith, here, is faithfulness.
Meekness is gentleness, strength that doesn't push. Temperance is self-control. In today's English, it sounds like someone you'd want to live next door to.
So is there no effort at all? Christians answer that differently. The same chapter says, "Walk in the Spirit."
Jesus, in John's Gospel, says: "I am the vine, ye are the branches," and the branch bears fruit by staying joined to the vine.
Prayer, worship, scripture, sacraments, serving others: in Christian teaching these keep the branch joined, like sun and rain. They don't manufacture fruit.

teach.h: AGAINST SUCH THERE IS NO LAW.
teach.b: And "against such there is no law" has a smile in it. Try picturing a court that bans patience.

how: Some Christians memorize the fruit of the Spirit from Galatians 5:22–23 and use the list to examine their lives.

games.q: what does “the fruit of the spirit” mean?
o: one fruit with many flavors, grown by the Spirit
the harvest gifts a church gives the poor
a list of rules that earn God's favor

games.q: old words, plain words — tap the pairs.
p: what Paul sets against the fruit

s: the verse says "the fruits of the Spirit are"
it says "the fruit of the Spirit is": one fruit, with many flavors.
Paul sets the fruit against "the works of the flesh"
just before the list he names the works of the flesh. works are made; fruit grows.
the fruit, like the gifts, goes to some people and not others
gifts are handed out differently; the fruit is pictured as growing in every life joined to the vine.

games.q: you want more patience. by this chapter's picture, what's the way?
o: grit your teeth and force it out.
stay joined to the vine and let it grow.
decide patience just isn't your gift.
games.why: "I am the vine, ye are the branches": in Christian teaching the branch bears fruit by staying joined. the chapter also says "walk in the Spirit": steps, not straining.

practice: Run slowly through the list, love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control, and notice which one tugs at you, maybe the one you're shortest on.
Don't plan to squeeze it out of yourself; picture one moment where it could grow, a long line, a slow reply, a hard conversation.
If you pray, ask for that fruit by name; if you don't, keep the one word with you, like a seed in a pocket.

wordCard.voice: The fruit of the Spirit. One fruit with many flavors, grown, not manufactured: love, joy, peace, and the rest.

orig.note: Greek: fruit — singular in Galatians 5:22, "the fruit of the Spirit is."

carryVoice: Your line: fruit, not effort. A gardener can't make an apple. Go gently.
